ruling: - **R42. Rulings get acted on, and main moves the way Anthropic moves its own.** Owner 13:39 CST Nov 11: "a report is still just a report yanno that's something for me to read rather than something to act upon". Read 13:41 CST: Anthropic's post "Redesigning source control at Anthropic" (Oct 13, updated Oct 15) says "A proper merge queue, for example, doesn't make much sense at agent scale". It tests after merge and before deploy, with automated bisect and revert. Its Claude Code team scales human approval by the change's risk and tracks reverts as the guard; a webinar on it runs Nov 18. Our batch flow holds a lock on main during each batch run (rule git-no-merge-during-batch-ci), and the baseline counts 147 lane drops in 15 batch merges. 1. A step that holds an owner ruling and has no lane is the coordinator's queue. It starts the step under rule parallelism-keep-going, not as a report line. Triage's reply names the step, and the sender's log item points to it, so the feedback guard proves it exists. 2. Proposed for stage 3, after a Plan agent and a refuter: a lane merges on its own green checks and its review, sized by risk. Main's CI runs after the merge; a red run bisects and reverts the breaking commit. Sessions install from a stable branch that moves only when main is green. 3. Guard numbers: reverts per merge, and the pace numbers. Main must first finish a CI run (#2591). Owner 13:43 CST: "lanes compete more for the machine isn't a real problem on cloud sessions where each spawns its own machine right? and then it is true for local machines though (which is why we have load brakes for local right" and "r42 part 2: i'm pretty open to this radical approach -- A". Part 1 stands on his 13:39 "A seems fine". Shared limits remain: the account's rate limit, CI runners, and agents inside one cloud container. The Plan agent's design for part 2 comes back to him. Design: docs/plans/r42-part2-design.md, branch claude/ecstatic-euler-capib9 (refuter: holds with changes). Owner 09:42 CST Nov 12, Q1: "none of the child repos are running rihgt now -- so if that makes A easier to do right now that's fine with me, and you'd just add all the repos in to that session". So all repos switch to per-lane merge together, and the lane session holds every repo. Owner 09:44 CST, Q2: "i'm fine with lanes moving a pr from draft to ready to run CI -- it's just it needed to be judgement based". A lane marks its PR ready once, after its last review, never per push. Owner 09:46 CST: "q3: is fine" (read as the third option: a red main stops merges only until the revert merges) and "q4: g is fine" (a revert is an ordinary lane PR merged with --base-red-ok). Owner 09:48 CST: "q3 correct" and "r42 -- yea that's correct yes?", his yes to the design with the refuter's changes. Lane merge-flow-after-anthropic starts, holding every repo; batching continues until its last act lands. Coordinator 13:51 CST: 70 ruled steps have no lane; the freeze (owner 09:18 CST Nov 10) allows fixes of items on main. Owner 13:50 CST: "remember my goal was to just have main in a state where it's stable enough to take on the full load of 70+ asks at once like my priority is max outcome speed". Owner 13:51 CST: "a". The freeze narrows: until the fan-out, only fixes that main's stability needs start (#2591, the mailbox fix, and failures in main's first finished run). Every other ruled step, fixes included, starts after the guard test file split, all at once.
